researchGoals.title: Geological History & Planetary Crust
researchGoals.description: Investigate impact cratering dynamics and volcanic flow stratigraphy to unravel Mars' crustal evolution.
researchGoals.focalQuestion: How did impacts and ancient volcanism shape the surface layers of Mars?

researchGoals.title: Water Reclamation & Operational Resilience
researchGoals.description: Master dust mitigation on power arrays and extract glacial ice resources for closed-loop ECLSS life support.
researchGoals.focalQuestion: How can an outpost survive dust deposition and harvest potable water reliably?

researchGoals.title: Ancient Habitable Environments & Biosignatures
researchGoals.description: Collect uncompromised lacustrine sediment cores and cryo-samples to search for organic chemical biosignatures.
researchGoals.focalQuestion: What geological signs tell us where past liquid water and life may have existed?

regions.name: Echo Crater
regions.landmark: Broken Radar Dome on Crater Rim
regions.pedagogicalQuestion: What clues link an impact event to the surrounding rocks and landscape?
regions.coreLesson: A strange rock is a clue. Its appearance alone cannot prove where it came from without chemical and orbital context.

focalPoints.title: Crater Rim & Ejecta Blanket
focalPoints.summary: Observe the raised rim and outward rays of pulverized rock thrown during meteoroid impact.
focalPoints.kidNote: Meteoroids hit Mars so hard they carve bowls and splash rocks outward like a puddle!
focalPoints.fieldNote: High-velocity shockwaves excavate target crust, depositing an inverted stratigraphy ejecta blanket.

focalPoints.title: Before & After Orbital Pair
focalPoints.summary: Match MRO HiRISE orbital satellite images taken before and after the fresh impact.
focalPoints.kidNote: Satellites orbiting Mars take pictures before and after an impact to spot fresh dark streaks.
focalPoints.fieldNote: Dark blast zones indicate dust displacement by meteoroid atmospheric shock front.

focalPoints.title: Candidate Meteorite vs Basalt
focalPoints.summary: Compare visual fusion crust and density metrics against surrounding Mars crustal rocks.
focalPoints.kidNote: Not every dark rock fell from space. Real meteorites often have a melted glassy crust.
focalPoints.fieldNote: Fusion crust forms during hypersonic atmospheric entry; olivine basalt lacks this quench texture.

optionalBranches.title: Crater Rim Panorama Perch
optionalBranches.benefit: Pins wide and close-up views side-by-side during seismic profile analysis.

optionalBranches.title: Sample Preservation Staging Point
optionalBranches.benefit: Highlights timestamp and seismic coordinates next to mystery impact profiles.

minigame.title: Seismic Impact Waveform Matcher
minigame.description: Match 3 recorded ground vibration profiles with their corresponding impact crater sites.

pairs.name: High-Frequency Chirp Event
pairs.clue: Sharp high-pitch acoustic sonification indicates a compact stony bolide impact.

pairs.name: Dispersed Multi-Ring Rumble
pairs.clue: Broad low rumbling reverberation reflects an impact into layered sedimentary crust.

pairs.name: Double Blast Atmospheric Wave
pairs.clue: Twin bursts show meteoroid fragmentation before impacting the surface as a cluster.

secondaryJobs.title: Protected Nitrogen-Sealed Sample Vault
secondaryJobs.description: Install hermetic nitrogen lockers to preserve delicate meteorite samples for deep Earth laboratory analysis.
secondaryJobs.readout: Sample specimens secured in hermetic sealed vaults. Pristine preservation ensured.

secondaryJobs.title: Accessible Workspace Sample Racks
secondaryJobs.description: Mount open-access racks next to the analytical mass spectrometer for instant comparison during sorties.
secondaryJobs.readout: Specimens mounted on instant analysis racks beside microscope.

regions.name: Wind Basin
regions.landmark: Anemometer Wind Tower & Solar Array Mast
regions.pedagogicalQuestion: How do wind patterns move fine dust, and how does dust affect solar energy systems?
regions.coreLesson: Dust can dim the sky and cover equipment. Engineering models help us simulate particle movement before storms hit.

focalPoints.title: Wind Shadows Behind Boulders
focalPoints.summary: Inspect elongated sand streaks formed in the aerodynamic wake behind basalt rocks.
focalPoints.kidNote: Just like hiding behind a wall from the wind, dust piles up behind rocks where the air is calm.
focalPoints.fieldNote: Lee-side deceleration creates deposition zones indicating prevailing storm azimuths.

focalPoints.title: Clean vs Dusted Solar Mast
focalPoints.summary: Measure light transmission drop on dusted solar glass panels compared to wiped sensors.
focalPoints.kidNote: Even a thin layer of red Mars dust can block half the sunlight our solar panels need!
focalPoints.fieldNote: Fine iron-oxide dust (particle size < 5 microns) causes optical extinction and power loss.

focalPoints.title: Dust Devil Tracks vs Global Storm
focalPoints.summary: Distinguish localized mini convective vortices from planet-wide dust hazes.
focalPoints.kidNote: Dust devils leave dark curvy tracks on the ground, while giant storms turn the whole sky orange.
focalPoints.fieldNote: Convective thermal columns scrub dust, exposing darker underlying substrate.

optionalBranches.title: Dune Crest Observation Point
optionalBranches.benefit: Displays inlet and exhaust directional arrows directly on the model grid.

optionalBranches.title: Space Weather Comparison Lab
optionalBranches.benefit: Enables single-step airflow visualization before committing the full model run.

minigame.title: Dust Particle Flow Pathway Model
minigame.description: Rotate 3x3 aerodynamic baffle tiles to guide clean filtered airflow from inlet to intake filter while avoiding clogged obstacles.

secondaryJobs.title: Solar Array Dust Sweeping Protocol
secondaryJobs.description: Deploy automated brush arms across primary photovoltaic masts. Yields +2 EU reserve energy recharge.
secondaryJobs.readout: Solar arrays polished clean. Energy generation boosted (+2 EU post-shift reserve).

secondaryJobs.title: Atmospheric Moisture Recovery Cycle
secondaryJobs.description: Recycle 2 units of condensation greywater into certified ultra-pure potable water (+2 Clean Water).
secondaryJobs.readout: Greywater batch processed and sanitized (+2 Clean Water certified).

regions.name: Black Rock Terrace
regions.landmark: Survey Truss Bridge across Ancient Lava Channel
regions.roverTool: Low-Angle Chassis Camera & Rock Illumination Array
regions.pedagogicalQuestion: How does rock layer superposition reveal the chronological timeline of ancient volcanic eruptions?
regions.coreLesson: A layer on top was laid down later than the layer beneath it. Relative order tells history without needing rock dates.

focalPoints.title: Lava Sheet Superposition Margin
focalPoints.summary: Inspect the direct boundary where a dark vesicular basalt flow caps an oxidized older bench.
focalPoints.kidNote: When lava spills over an older rock, the new lava hardens on top. Top is younger!
focalPoints.fieldNote: Law of Superposition: Undeformed sedimentary and extrusive volcanic strata place younger units above older.

focalPoints.title: Collapsed Lava Tube Channel
focalPoints.summary: Trace a sinuous rille carved by underground magma rivers where the roof has collapsed.
focalPoints.kidNote: Underground lava rivers left hollow tunnels. Today, hollow tubes could protect astronauts from space radiation!
focalPoints.fieldNote: Intact lava tubes provide several meters of regolith shielding, attenuating GCR and SPE radiation.

focalPoints.title: Vesicular Basalt vs Pyroclastic Ash
focalPoints.summary: Compare gas bubble vesicles in cooled lava against fine-grained volcanic ash tuff.
focalPoints.kidNote: Little holes inside volcanic rocks are bubbles where hot gas escaped as the rock froze solid.
focalPoints.fieldNote: Vesicle density indicates volatile content and atmospheric pressure during effusive extrusion.

optionalBranches.title: Sinuous Channel Lookout
optionalBranches.benefit: Marks the clearest cross-cutting contact edge with an illuminated trace.

optionalBranches.title: Lava Tube Habitat Vault Study
optionalBranches.benefit: Unlocks a clear 2D cutaway diagram showing subterranean lava layer ordering.

minigame.title: Lava Layer Chronology Ordering
minigame.description: Arrange 4 geological flow units (A, B, C, D) in order from OLDEST (Deepest) to YOUNGEST (Uppermost).

layers.name: Flow Unit A (Vesicular Basalt)
layers.clue: Lies directly underneath Flow C, but cuts over Flow B.

layers.name: Flow Unit B (Oxidized Red Regolith)
layers.clue: Baked by hot magma from Unit A; lies above bedrock Unit D.

layers.name: Flow Unit C (Columnar Jointed Cap)
layers.clue: The top-most surface layer exposed to the open Mars sky.

layers.name: Flow Unit D (Dense Olivine Base)
layers.clue: Found at the bottom-most floor of the collapsed canyon.

secondaryJobs.title: Passive Aerogel Thermal Insulation Barrier
secondaryJobs.description: Wrap habitat bulkheads in silica aerogel blankets to prevent overnight thermal leakage.
secondaryJobs.readout: Passive aerogel shields installed. Night thermal loss reduced by 40%.

secondaryJobs.title: Active Specimen Workbench Heating Coil
secondaryJobs.description: Install resistive warming coils along scientific datapad tables for rapid instrument startup.
secondaryJobs.readout: Active workbench heaters powered. Scientific instrumentation warmed for instant use.

regions.name: Sealed Ice Cliff
regions.landmark: Glacial Core Drill Rig on Scarp Face
regions.pedagogicalQuestion: How do we sample subsurface glacier ice, and why is raw ice different from treated drinking water?
regions.coreLesson: An ice core is a scientific sample of ancient climate. Safe drinking water requires its own purification steps and chemical tests.

focalPoints.title: Protective Debris Mantle
focalPoints.summary: Examine the 1-meter thick dust and gravel coat that shields buried ice from sublimating into space.
focalPoints.kidNote: Without this blanket of red dust, Mars ice would turn straight into gas and blow away into space!
focalPoints.fieldNote: Low atmospheric pressure (600 Pa) causes direct solid-to-gas sublimation unless shielded by lag regolith.

focalPoints.title: SHARAD Orbital Radar Profile
focalPoints.summary: Inspect orbital radar reflections revealing a 90% pure subsurface water ice sheet 80 meters thick.
focalPoints.kidNote: Radar satellites send radio pulses deep underground to bounce off pure water ice.
focalPoints.fieldNote: Shallow Radar (SHARAD) dielectric constant (~3.1) confirms pure massive water ice deposit.

focalPoints.title: Water Ice (H2O) vs Dry Ice (CO2)
focalPoints.summary: Measure sublimation temperature thresholds distinguishing seasonal carbon dioxide frost from water ice.
focalPoints.kidNote: Dry ice is frozen carbon dioxide (-125°C). Water ice (-0°C) is what humans need to drink!
focalPoints.fieldNote: CO2 frost sublimates rapidly during spring equinox; H2O ice remains locked in cryogenic permafrost.

optionalBranches.benefit: Expands ultrasonic drill operating sweet spot from 30-70% to 20-80% tolerance.

optionalBranches.benefit: Displays Advance -> Check -> Seal guidance overlay during core acquisition.

minigame.description: Maintain core drill motor pressure within safe 30%–70% speed band, tag depth markers, and seal container.

steps.label: Advance Drill Bit
steps.description: Engage rotation and penetrate through 1m protective debris mantle.

steps.label: Extract Cryo Core
steps.description: Capture unfragmented 30cm banded glacial water ice sample.

steps.label: Label & Seal Container
steps.description: Apply cryogenic thermal seal and barcoded depth registry tag.

secondaryJobs.title: Subsurface Core Stratigraphy Analysis
secondaryJobs.description: Feed extracted ice core through multi-spectral laser scanner to reconstruct 500,000-year climate record.
secondaryJobs.readout: Glacial ice core scanned. Prehistoric atmospheric climate layers cataloged.

secondaryJobs.title: ECLSS Greywater Filtration Run
secondaryJobs.description: Process station greywater holding tank through catalytic oxidizer to yield +2 certified potable water.
secondaryJobs.readout: ECLSS filtration run complete. Clean reserve water stock increased (+2 Clean Water).

regions.name: Ancient Lake Shore
regions.landmark: Telemetry Transceiver Arch on Dry Delta
regions.roverTool: Robotic Arm with Microscopic Imager & Witness Tube
regions.pedagogicalQuestion: What scientific documentation does a geological clue require before scientists can study it on Earth?
regions.coreLesson: A useful clue deserves careful study. It does not prove that life once lived here without clean provenance and proof.

focalPoints.title: Delta Mudstone Cross-Bedding
focalPoints.summary: Inspect fine ripple layers deposited by slow-moving liquid water in an ancient Martian lake.
focalPoints.kidNote: Smooth mud layers show that water once flowed gently here billions of years ago!
focalPoints.fieldNote: Fine-grained smectite clay mudstones possess high potential for preserving ancient organic biosignatures.

focalPoints.title: Robotic Coring Arm & Turret
focalPoints.summary: Test robotic arm degrees of freedom, rotary percussive drill, and dust-removal gas puffer.
focalPoints.kidNote: The robot's arm works like a careful scientist with a magnifying glass and camera.
focalPoints.fieldNote: 5-DoF robotic arm positions SHERLOC and PIXL instruments with sub-millimeter precision.

focalPoints.title: Witness Tube Contamination Check
focalPoints.summary: Audit hermetic witness tubes designed to catch Earth contaminants and ensure sample integrity.
focalPoints.kidNote: Witness tubes are clean empty tubes that prove Earth dust didn't sneak into our Mars rocks!
focalPoints.fieldNote: Witness blanks capture outgassing volatiles and rover contaminants to validate true Mars origin.

optionalBranches.benefit: Enables automatic verification checklist for Wide Angle, Micro-texture, and Coordinates.

targets.clue: Organic-bearing mudstone candidate requiring strict witness tube verification.

scientificSources.title: NASA's InSight Hears Its First Meteoroid Impacts on Mars
scientificSources.keyFact: InSight's seismometer detected distinct acoustic seismic waves from four space rocks crashing into Mars.
scientificSources.interpretationBoundary: Seismic amplitudes correlate with ground transmission distance, not exclusively impactor diameter.

scientificSources.title: Orbital Verification of Fresh Martian Impact Craters
scientificSources.keyFact: HiRISE satellite images verify ground craters matched from seismic coordinates down to sub-meter resolution.
scientificSources.interpretationBoundary: Orbital imagery captures surface albedo shifts; subterranean disruption requires radar or seismic modeling.

scientificSources.title: Identifying Meteorites on the Martian Surface
scientificSources.keyFact: Meteorites discovered by rovers feature melted aerodynamic fusion crusts distinct from local oxidized volcanic rocks.
scientificSources.interpretationBoundary: Visual color or magnetism alone cannot verify extraterrestrial origin without elemental spectroscopy.

scientificSources.title: The Fact and Fiction of Martian Dust Storms
scientificSources.keyFact: Martian atmosphere is 1% of Earth's density. Even 60 mph winds carry little force, but fine dust blocks sunlight.
scientificSources.interpretationBoundary: Martian storms cannot overturn buildings or heavy landers; their hazard is optical obscuration and solar starvation.

scientificSources.title: Dust Accumulation and Cleaning Events on Solar Panels
scientificSources.keyFact: Over 14 years, Opportunity survived by monitoring solar array dust deposition and occasional wind cleaning events.
scientificSources.interpretationBoundary: Wind cleaning is unpredictable and cannot replace engineered dust mitigation protocols.

scientificSources.title: Global Dust Storm Dynamics on Mars
scientificSources.keyFact: Regional dust storms can loft aerosol particles 50 km high, triggering planet-encircling thermal warming cycles.
scientificSources.interpretationBoundary: Space weather solar flare events are distinct from lower tropospheric atmospheric dust transport.

scientificSources.mission: High Resolution Stereo Camera (Mars Express) & MRO
scientificSources.title: Lava Flows and Caldera Collapse on Mars
scientificSources.credit: ESA / DLR / FU Berlin / NASA JPL
scientificSources.keyFact: Sinuous basalt lava flows near Olympus Mons preserve distinct cooling margins demonstrating stratigraphic superposition.
scientificSources.interpretationBoundary: Superposition provides relative sequence of events; numerical age dates require radiometric isotopic analysis.

scientificSources.title: Lava Tubes as Potential Human Habitats on the Moon and Mars
scientificSources.keyFact: Subsurface lava tube roofs block galactic cosmic rays (GCR) and solar particle events (SPE), offering natural shielding.
scientificSources.interpretationBoundary: Natural lava tubes require structural integrity inspection for micrometeorite breach vulnerabilities.

scientificSources.title: Igneous Petrology and Volcanic Rocks of Mars
scientificSources.keyFact: Vesicular basalt samples document low-viscosity effusive volcanism with escaping gas bubbles in ancient Martian history.
scientificSources.interpretationBoundary: Rock texture identifies eruptive style, not the duration of the entire volcanic volcanic province.

scientificSources.title: Glacial Ice Deposits in Mid-Latitudes of Mars
scientificSources.credit: NASA / JPL-Caltech / ASI / Univ. of Rome
scientificSources.keyFact: Radar sounding reveals massive glaciers protected under 1 to 2 meters of rocky debris mantle across mid-latitudes.
scientificSources.interpretationBoundary: Subsurface ice cannot be scooped like fresh snow; it is frozen into cryogenic rocky permafrost concrete.

scientificSources.title: Mapping Dielectric Properties of Subsurface Ice
scientificSources.keyFact: Radio radar pulses penetrate hundreds of meters through rock, reflecting sharply at pure water ice interfaces.
scientificSources.interpretationBoundary: Radar profiles map dielectric contrasts, which must be calibrated with core drilling for physical confirmation.

scientificSources.title: Dry Ice Sublimation Dynamics on the Martian Poles and Slopes
scientificSources.keyFact: Carbon dioxide freezes directly from air at -125°C, forming seasonal dry ice frost that sublimates in spring.
scientificSources.interpretationBoundary: CO2 dry ice is toxic and unusable for human hydration; it must not be confused with perennial H2O water ice.

scientificSources.title: Astrobiology and Delta Sedimentology at Jezero Crater
scientificSources.keyFact: Ancient river delta siltstones in Jezero crater formed 3.5 billion years ago under sustained standing liquid water.
scientificSources.interpretationBoundary: Fluvial sediment layers prove past liquid water, but do not automatically prove past microscopic life.

scientificSources.title: Robotic Coring and Contamination Control Architecture
scientificSources.keyFact: The 2-meter robotic arm uses coring bits, gas dust removal tools, and micro-imagers to certify sample provenance.
scientificSources.interpretationBoundary: Robotic instruments provide preliminary triage; final biosignature confirmation requires Earth laboratory mass spectrometers.

scientificSources.title: Witness Tubes for Contamination Tracking in Mars Samples
scientificSources.keyFact: Witness tubes contain pristine materials opened on Mars to document any chemical contamination brought from Earth.
scientificSources.interpretationBoundary: Witness tubes monitor Earth contamination; they are blanks, not actual Mars geological rock samples.

scientificSources.title: NASA Achieves 98% Water Recovery Milestone on International Space Station
scientificSources.keyFact: Advanced distillation and catalytic oxidizers recover 98% of astronaut sweat and urine as ultrapure drinking water.
scientificSources.interpretationBoundary: ISS zero-gravity centrifugal recovery systems require redesign for 38% Martian surface gravity.

scientificSources.title: Junior Astronaut Training Program & Nutrition Toolkits
scientificSources.keyFact: STEM training modules teach cadets how nutrition, exercise, and mental teamwork sustain crew health on long space voyages.
scientificSources.interpretationBoundary: Educational food models illustrate dietary variety; closed-loop bio-regenerative life support is an ongoing engineering challenge.
